quote: That that the the Tesla panels, they that's something only Tesla does. We're a certified Tesla arm installer, but only for their batteries.
stewart_read: Rep correctly reframes the Tesla panel confusion — clarifying Ion installs batteries (Powerwall) for Tesla, not panels or shingles — matching the schema's guidance to reframe cleanly only when the customer raises the expectation gap.
coaching_implication: This is a clean example of the correct reframe; can be used as a positive clip for training other setters on the Tesla expectation gap.

quote: I I'm taking a look, and it looks like you have too much shade for us to make our system work anyway. So I'll just get back to us for now.
stewart_read: This reads as a legitimate tool-based disqualification, not an unaudited fast exit — the customer's very next lines (01:47-02:00) independently confirm a prior installer flagged the same shade/placement issue at this address and rejected his proposed rack workaround, which corroborates the DQ.
alternative_hypothesis: A reactive read would say the rep pulled the plug too fast without giving the customer a chance to discuss workarounds — but the customer's own corroborating account undercuts that read; there is no dedicated shade-DQ schema item, so this is scored against dq_rules generally rather than a specific verify subsection.
coaching_implication: No coaching action needed here — flag this as a case where quick tool-based disqualification was validated by the customer's own history, useful as a reference point for what a legitimate fast DQ looks like.

quote: I know that there is, like, a two year back, wait period currently, I believe, with the with the at least their equipment.
stewart_read: Rep states a specific two-year wait-period figure for Tesla equipment while hedging with 'I believe' — this is an admit-and-hedge pattern rather than fabrication, but the specific number is unverified.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to either confirm this figure before stating it as fact, or drop the specific number and simply say wait times vary — hedged specifics can still mislead the customer.

quote: Yeah. Unfortunately, my company, we also only do roof mounted systems, so I apologize about that as well.
stewart_read: Rep transparently states a second disqualifying constraint (no ground-mount option) rather than leaving the DQ vague, which is honest handling of a hard no.
coaching_implication: Nothing to fix here — clear, honest communication of a real product limitation.

quote: Not usually. I mean, it's it's their their main thing is the shingles right now.
stewart_read: After the DQ was already delivered, the customer asks a benign closing-courtesy question about Tesla panel capacity; the rep answers briefly and accurately. This is low-risk goodwill conversation with a disqualified lead, not a scope-creep sales debate with an active prospect.
alternative_hypothesis: A stricter read would call this setter_scope_creep since the rep is explaining product capacity detail — but there is no appointment or sale at stake post-DQ, so the downside is negligible and this is not a coaching priority.
coaching_implication: No action needed; if anything, this maintained rapport and left the customer satisfied ('That's all you answered all my questions'), which is a fine way to close a DQ call.

quote: And, what got you interested in looking at solar?
stewart_read: Rep asks the required interest question early and gets a real answer about Tesla panel confusion and a prior solar quote, which is exactly the kind of competitive context the schema wants surfaced.
coaching_implication: Good practice — interest question was asked before the DQ occurred, so the qualifying info was captured even though the call ended without an appointment.

quote: I talked to somebody about a week or two ago about solar, and it was, like, they wanted, like, 12 panels or something.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior solar conversation with another company (quote of ~12 panels) but the rep never asks which company or what happened with that quote before pivoting to the Tesla clarification.
alternative_hypothesis: Since the call ends in a DQ minutes later, probing this competitive detail would have had limited immediate payoff — but it still would have been free information for the record.
coaching_implication: Minor: coach the rep to spend 10-15 seconds asking 'who was that with?' when a customer casually references a prior quote, even on calls that end up disqualified, since Ion may re-contact this lead later.
